extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO discipline staff, and respondents in USPTO reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal disciplinary sanctions on a registered patent practitioner based on a state-law suspension. Covers notice, opportunity to respond, grounds for suspension, and the specific orders imposed by the USPTO (publication, dissociation from customer numbers, duties during suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO OED files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and issues a Notice and Order; the Notice provides an opportunity to respond within the time provided (here, forty (40) days). If no genuine issue of material fact exists under § 11.24(d), identical reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposing reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order explains the right to respond and identifies § 11.24(d)(1) as the governing provision for opposition; absence of a response may result in determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — predicate for USPTO action
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline under USPTO regulation is predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state suspension for professional misconduct can serve as the regulatory basis for USPTO discipline under § 11.804(h); the Final Order cites the Massachusetts suspension as the predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law (Mass. R. Prof. C. 5.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary ground: unauthorized practice of law in Ohio in violation of Mass. R. Prof. C. 5.5(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state finding of unauthorized practice was one of the bases for the Massachusetts suspension and thus for the USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper firm name/letterhead (Mass. R. Prof. C. 7.1 and 7.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary ground: using a firm name and letterhead with an address in Ohio in violation of Mass. R. Prof. C. 7.1 and 7.5(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such misrepresentations in firm identification formed part of the misconduct that led to suspension by the state court and supports reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal convictions as professional misconduct (Mass. R. Prof. C. 8.4(b) and (h))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary ground: convictions of misdemeanors (reckless operation of vehicles and possession of marijuana) described as violating Mass. R. Prof. C. 8.4(b) and (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions can constitute professional misconduct under the applicable state professional conduct rules and therefore be a basis for discipline by both state authorities and the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to report convictions (Mass. R. Prof. C. 8.4(d) and S.J.C. Rule 4:01, § 12(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary ground: failure to report convictions to bar counsel in violation of Mass. R. Prof. C. 8.4(d) and S.J.C. Rule 4:01, § 12(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omissions to report required information to bar authorities are cited as independent grounds supporting state suspension and thus reciprocal USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension term and scope (six months; practice before USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO ordered suspension from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO for six (6) months, identical in duration to the state suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the effective term and scope (all practice before the USPTO, including patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) and ties the sanction to the state-imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (Official Gazette, OED Reading Room, 37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states of admission, courts of admission, and the public; disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes the exact Notice language to be published and references where disciplinary decisions are publicly accessible (e-FOIA OED Reading Room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not recite § 11.58's text, it explicitly requires compliance with those duties (e.g., notification and client protection obligations set out in § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, the Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a Customer Number, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, which provide the USPTO's authority to discipline practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders will cite these authorities as the legal basis for reciprocal discipline and related enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order within the prescribed time, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly notes the Respondent's lack of response and relies on that failure in reaching the determination to suspend.
